Thanks for this, it's a clean, well-scoped fix. Pulling the lookup into `catalogVariantLookup.ts` reads nicely, and returning a bare `{ id }` row on 403 (rather than `null`) is the right call: on the SKU page a `null` would have dropped into the "not found" branch instead of rendering the WMS data. Sending `x-om-forbidden-redirect: 0` follows the existing pattern, gets rid of the misleading "admin role" toast for this lookup, and the end-to-end test through the real `apiCall`/`apiFetch` shows the header is actually needed. Other failures still go through `raiseCrudError`, which is good.

One small, non-blocking thought: for a WMS-only user the SKU page header still shows the raw variant UUID. `/api/wms/inventory/balances` and `/api/wms/inventory/movements` already come back with `variant_sku`/`variant_name` (via `attachVariantLabelsToListItems`, gated by `wms.view`), so the page could fall back to those before the id. That's what the issue's expected result suggests, and it's fine as a follow-up if you'd rather keep this PR small. There's also a tiny test nit inline. Approving from my side once CI has run on this head.

review_comments.body: Nit: `headers` is never used, and the comment on the next line suggests the mock branches on the opt-out header, but it doesn't (the 403 to `ForbiddenError` conversion happens in `apiFetch`, which is what the test is really checking). Could drop the variable and reword the comment so the next reader isn't confused.
